rationale: Astra is the clearest chapter entry because it keeps artifact and approval side by side, blocks B with approval for A, then opens the executor only after B is reviewed. Baseline adds a different check: production prerequisites can change while an approved migration waits. Fable is a complementary LangGraph implementation lesson about repeated side effects on resume, best watched after the approval-boundary example.
findings: Astra 00:09.5–00:14.5 directly demonstrates the guide’s artifact-substitution problem: B reaches an executor holding approval A and the barrier stays closed. Baseline 00:14.1–00:18.7 instead blocks a correctly identified migration because production changed from its expected v8 to v9; these mechanisms are complementary, not interchangeable.

Astra 00:17–00:25.6 completes recovery through fresh review, B = B, and visible deployment. Baseline 00:21.1–00:24.4 ends safely at REVIEW REQUIRED; that is an accurate unresolved handoff, but offers less guidance on completing the workflow.

Baseline 00:01–00:08.5 establishes a normal success and shows target/schema context in a durable checkpoint. Its checkpoint rows at 00:05.3 and 00:18.7 take more effort to read at 350px than Astra’s large artifact/approval pairing at 00:13.8; the cause of Baseline’s external state change remains implicit.

Fable 00:07.7–00:09.4 makes LangGraph node replay concrete with a returning cursor and two notification rows. Its reordered example at 00:21.9–00:24.5 shows one notification after approval; this is one ordinary resume, not an exactly-once guarantee across later failures or retries. Neither other cut teaches this implementation hazard.

Fable’s original packet/label collision near 00:08.8 and unexplained reset near 00:15 were corrected. The final cut keeps the node label clear, names LangGraph in the subtitle, and fades between examples at 00:14.6–00:15.9 before showing the operation reorder through 00:16.8; the reset no longer reads as a production rollback.

Astra spends roughly 00:00–00:04 on preparation before reaching its central approval comparison; Baseline’s blocked ending holds roughly 00:21.5–00:24.5. These are modest pacing costs, while Fable fits two denser sequences into 30.2 seconds and benefits most from pausing or replaying. All three provide readable settled outcomes and matching first/last frames.
contentVerdict: Keep as core. Teams expanding agent tool access need an enforced approval boundary and a reviewable artifact, target and evidence packet before consequential execution. The guide builds appropriately on guardrails-and-permissions and gives an observable sandbox exercise for stale approval and duplicate resumption. LangGraph replay is a useful implementation-specific reference within this core topic; it does not make the whole topic optional. The guide explicitly separates protected decisions, durable storage, execution-time revalidation and retry safety, and does not promise these from a prompt or framework alone.

limitations: Audio was analysed using decoded floating-point peaks, spectrograms and energy around scheduled cues; it was not heard. Overlapping cue windows do not prove perceptual separation or quality.
Visual review used decoded contact sheets across the complete durations, full-resolution beat frames, 350px frames and exact first/last frames. No continuous real-time playback is claimed.

These are illustrative animations, not security or integration tests of a working executor. No cut depicts the complete authenticated-review, target-binding, concurrency, rejection/cancellation and retry contract; the guide carries those boundaries.
Scores apply to the final encoded cuts and their stated scope. A high accuracy score does not imply comprehensive coverage or production readiness.
The saved recommendation is an editorial recommendation; no shared default-selection, Git or publication operation was performed.
